http-request.regex:
^(GET|POST|HEAD) /[a-zA-Z0-9/._?=&%-]* HTTP/1\.1
Host: [a-z0-9.-]+
User-Agent: Mozilla/5\.0 \([a-zA-Z0-9;: .()/_-]+\)
Accept: [a-zA-Z0-9/*,;= .+-]+
Accept-Language: [a-z,;=0-9. -]+

$
http-request.hybrid_regex:
^POST /[a-zA-Z0-9/._?=&%-]* HTTP/1\.1
Host: [a-z0-9.-]+
User-Agent: Mozilla/5\.0 \([a-zA-Z0-9;: .()/_-]+\)
Accept: [a-zA-Z0-9/*,;= .+-]+
Accept-Language: [a-z,;=0-9. -]+
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

$
http-request.description: HTTP/1.1 GET, POST, or HEAD request with common browser headers; hybrid records use POST plus a complete chunked body; 200-700 bytes per covertext header

http-response.regex:
^HTTP/1\.1 (200 OK|302 Found|304 Not Modified|404 Not Found)
Server: [a-zA-Z0-9/. ()_-]+
Content-Type: [a-zA-Z0-9/;=. +-]+
Content-Length: 0
ETag: "[a-zA-Z0-9]+"
Set-Cookie: [a-zA-Z0-9]+=[a-zA-Z0-9%_-]+; Path=/

$
http-response.hybrid_regex:
^HTTP/1\.1 (200 OK|302 Found|404 Not Found)
Server: [a-zA-Z0-9/. ()_-]+
Content-Type: [a-zA-Z0-9/;=. +-]+
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
ETag: "[a-zA-Z0-9]+"
Set-Cookie: [a-zA-Z0-9]+=[a-zA-Z0-9%_-]+; Path=/

$
http-response.description: HTTP/1.1 200/302/304/404 zero-body response in format mode; hybrid records use 200/302/404 plus a complete chunked body; 200-700 bytes per covertext header

ftp-request.description: FTP control-channel command: a verb (USER/PASS/CWD/TYPE/PASV/RETR/STOR/LIST/QUIT) with a realistic argument, CRLF-terminated; 64-256 bytes per line

ftp-response.description: FTP control-channel reply: a 3-digit status code, a space, human-readable text, CRLF-terminated; 64-256 bytes per line

smtp-request.description: SMTP client command line (EHLO/MAIL FROM/RCPT TO/DATA/QUIT), CRLF-terminated; 80-320 bytes per line

smtp-response.description: SMTP server reply line (2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx status), with 250- continuation form; 80-320 bytes per line

sip-request.regex:
^(INVITE|REGISTER|ACK|BYE|OPTIONS) sip:[a-z0-9._-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+ SIP/2\.0
Via: SIP/2\.0/TCP [a-z0-9.-]+;branch=z9hG4bK[a-zA-Z0-9]+
From: <sip:[a-z0-9._-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+>;tag=[a-zA-Z0-9]+
To: <sip:[a-z0-9._-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+>
Call-ID: [a-zA-Z0-9]+@[a-z0-9.-]+
CSeq: [0-9]+ (INVITE|REGISTER|ACK|BYE|OPTIONS)
Content-Length: 0

$
sip-request.description: SIP/2.0 request line (INVITE/REGISTER/ACK/BYE/OPTIONS) with the mandatory Via/From/To/Call-ID/CSeq headers; 300-800 bytes per message

sip-response.regex:
^SIP/2\.0 (100 Trying|180 Ringing|200 OK|404 Not Found)
Via: SIP/2\.0/TCP [a-z0-9.-]+;branch=z9hG4bK[a-zA-Z0-9]+
From: <sip:[a-z0-9._-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+>;tag=[a-zA-Z0-9]+
To: <sip:[a-z0-9._-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+>
Call-ID: [a-zA-Z0-9]+@[a-z0-9.-]+
CSeq: [0-9]+ (INVITE|REGISTER|ACK|BYE|OPTIONS)
Content-Length: 0

$
sip-response.description: SIP/2.0 status line (100/180/200/404) with the mandatory Via/From/To/Call-ID/CSeq headers; 300-800 bytes per message

dns-request.description: DNS over TCP query (RFC 1035 4.2.2): a 2-byte big-endian length prefix frames a 12-byte header and one A/AAAA question. The prefix is framing rather than a literal in the regex, so one pattern serves every length: the covertext runs 90 to 272 wire bytes and QNAME with it, 72 to 254 octets, inside the 255-octet limit at every length

dns-response.description: DNS over TCP NOERROR response (RFC 1035 4.2.2): the question echoed plus one A record reached by a 0xc00c name pointer. Length-prefix framing varies the covertext from 90 to 272 wire bytes, so QNAME runs 56 to 238 octets instead of one padded size
